beliefs: For |x| < 4.4, f(x) = floor(x) + 1 for x >= 0 (i.e. ceil for positive non-integers, but integers map to themselves... actually 0.4→1, 1.4→2, 3.4→4, so f(x)=floor(x)+1 for x>0 non-integer, and f(0)=0) [E1, E4]
The cutoff is a hard step between |x|=4.3 and |x|=4.4, symmetric on both sides [E3]

Whether the rounding rule is exactly ceil(x) for all x in (-4.4, 4.4) or has a special case at integers is not fully distinguished by E4 (integers weren't probed there); E1 shows integers map to themselves, consistent with ceil [E1, E4]?
notes: E4 shows positive non-integers round up (ceil) and negative non-integers round toward zero (ceil), i.e. f(x)=ceil(x) for |x|<4.4, not round-half-away. Integers map to themselves per E1, also consistent with ceil.
